```python
# Unit test for function generate_integers
def test_generate_integers():
    # Basic case: even numbers between 2 and 8
    assert generate_integers(2, 8) == [2, 4, 6, 8]

    # Reversed arguments should yield the same result
    assert generate_integers(8, 2) == [2, 4, 6, 8]

    # Range clamped to [2, 8]
    assert generate_integers(1, 10) == [2, 4, 6, 8]
    assert generate_integers(0, 100) == [2, 4, 6, 8]

    # Partial clamping: lower bound raised to 2
    assert generate_integers(1, 4) == [2, 4]

    # Partial clamping: upper bound capped at 8
    assert generate_integers(6, 10) == [6, 8]

    # Range with no even numbers after clamping (upper < lower)
    assert generate_integers(9, 10) == []
    assert generate_integers(10, 20) == []

    # Negative inputs: lower clamped to 2, upper below lower -> empty
    assert generate_integers(-2, -1) == []
    assert generate_integers(-10, 0) == []

    # Single-value ranges
    assert generate_integers(4, 4) == [4]   # even single value
    assert generate_integers(3, 3) == []    # odd single value
    assert generate_integers(7, 7) == []

    # Small ranges containing one even number
    assert generate_integers(1, 3) == [2]
    assert generate_integers(2, 3) == [2]
    assert generate_integers(3, 6) == [4, 6]
    assert generate_integers(5, 6) == [6]

    # Overlapping ranges around the clamp boundaries
    assert generate_integers(2, 2) == [2]
    assert generate_integers(8, 8) == [8]
    assert generate_integers(1, 2) == [2]
    assert generate_integers(8, 9) == [8]

    print("All tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_generate_integers()
```
